claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule reached speeds of approximately 25,000 mph (roughly 40,000 km/h) during its return to Earth on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule hit top speeds of approximately 25,000 mph while re-entering the Earth's atmosphere.
The Artemis II Orion capsule endured temperatures of nearly 5,000°F (2,760°C) while re-entering the Earth's atmosphere.
The Artemis II Orion capsule entered the atmosphere at nearly 25,000 mph to splash down in the Pacific Ocean.
The SLS rocket traveled at over 17,000 mph to reach orbit.
While coasting to the Moon, the speed of the Artemis II spacecraft varied, sometimes dropping to a few thousand miles per hour, as shown on the NASA Artemis II tracker.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II spacecraft performed a "skip-entry" maneuver during the mission.
The Artemis II spacecraft had a splashdown speed of about 15 mph
